title: 9th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened with 42 members present. Three ministers and the Attorney General answered written questions, which were read into the record, and the President's letter changing the work areas of three ministries was sent to a committee, along with the list of four applicants for the Police Board. The main debate was the Judiciary Committee's report on a bill amending the Courts Act: opposition members argued the committee had not dealt with the Majlis Counsel General's comments and linked the bill to the Supreme Court bench, while the committee chair said the changes repeated earlier provisions. After repeated warnings the Speaker named three members and removed them from the chamber, then held a roll-call vote (the electronic system had a fault) and the bill passed 68 to 9. The Speaker announced Ramadan sitting hours and the next sitting on 3 March 2025.

items.outcome: written answer read; member disputed part of it; published unchanged

items.title: Judiciary Committee report on the bill to amend the Courts Act (Law 2010/22), submitted by the Holhudhoo member

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked how Saudi Hajj quotas are allocated; argued the Counsel General's comments on the courts bill must be decided on the floor before the bill is debated or voted.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said the Home Security minister had not been scheduled in 14 days; argued the courts bill amounts to changing the Supreme Court bench and ignored the Counsel General's advice.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked about the legal basis for ending the HDC-CMC reclamation agreement; said ministry replies on his letters were late; raised fear among residents after a killing on a small island.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Presented the Judiciary Committee report: the bill repeats provisions from an earlier amendment, no court has questioned them, and the committee passed it before the Counsel General's comments arrived.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Disputed the committee reporter's account of how the Counsel General's comments were to be handled and said the matter should go back to the floor.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Raised a point of order on his urgent question about the Holhudhoo death case and continuing protests; the chair said the matter was not within the recent-events rule.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said the Speaker's office should not have declined the Velidhoo urgent question and voiced concern about events on that island.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 4 to 6 accepted as no amendments were submitted.
Kendhoo member Mauroof Zakir placed on the Judiciary Committee in place of North Galolhu member Mohamed Ibrahim.
Urgent questions from the Velidhoo and Kanditheemu members were not taken up (Rule 197 conditions not met).
President's letter on the work areas of three ministries referred to the committee on government accountability.
List of four Police Board applicants referred to the Security Services Committee.
Courts Act (Law 2010/22) amendment bill passed 68-9 by roll call after the electronic voting system failed.
Three members (Vaikaradhoo, South Galolhu, Kendhoo) were named by the Speaker and removed from the chamber.
Ramadan sitting hours announced; next sitting set for Monday 3 March 2025 at 10:30.

votes.what: Passage of the bill amending the Courts Act (Law 2010/22), per the Judiciary Committee report; 79 members present, 39 needed to pass
